import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive insights
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price distribution by sensor type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_order = df.groupby('sensor_type')['price_usd'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='sensor_type', y='price_usd', order=sensor_order, palette='Set2', ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Price Distribution by Sensor Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Sensor Type', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# 2. Megapixels vs Price colored by sensor type
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    sensor_data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax2.scatter(sensor_data['megapixels'], sensor_data['price_usd'], 
               label=sensor, alpha=0.6, s=30)
ax2.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Megapixels vs Price', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left')
ax2.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Camera releases over time by brand
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(5).index
brand_year = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby(['model_year', 'brand']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
brand_year.plot(kind='line', marker='o', ax=ax3, linewidth=2, markersize=5)
ax3.set_title('Camera Releases Over Time (Top 5 Brands)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Models', fontsize=11)
ax3.legend(title='Brand', fontsize=9)
ax3.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 4. 4K Video capability distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
video_4k_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K Capable']
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4']
ax4.pie(video_4k_counts, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=colors)
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')

# 5. Weight vs Price by body type
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :2])
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
for body in body_types:
    body_data = df[df['body_type'] == body]
    ax5.scatter(body_data['weight_grams'], body_data['price_usd'], 
               label=body, alpha=0.6, s=40)
ax5.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11)
ax5.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax5.set_title('Weight vs Price by Body Type', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax5.legend(fontsize=9)
ax5.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 6. Average specs by brand (top 5)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
top_brands_df = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)]
avg_specs = top_brands_df.groupby('brand').agg({
    'megapixels': 'mean',
    'price_usd': 'mean'
}).sort_values('price_usd', ascending=True)

y_pos = np.arange(len(avg_specs))
ax6.barh(y_pos, avg_specs['price_usd'], color='steelblue', alpha=0.7)
ax6.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax6.set_yticklabels(avg_specs.index)
ax6.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax6.set_title('Average Price by Brand\n(Top 5)', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax6.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# Overall title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis - Comprehensive Overview', 
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
